title: Camelcase Matching
statement:
You get a list of words `queries` and a word `pattern`. A query **matches** the pattern when it can be produced from `pattern` by adding zero or more lowercase English letters at any places (front, end or between characters). Characters of `pattern` keep their order and may not be dropped or changed, and no uppercase letter may be added.

Return a list of booleans of the same length as `queries` whose `i`-th entry is `true` exactly when `queries[i]` matches `pattern`.
constraints: queries[i] and pattern contain only English letters (upper or lower case)
notes:
## Intuition

A query matches when `pattern` appears in it as a subsequence and every letter of the query that is *not* used by that subsequence is lowercase. The hints suggest a DP over (query position, pattern position), but a single left-to-right scan is enough: whenever the query's next letter equals the next unmatched pattern letter, using it right away is never worse than saving it, and any other uppercase letter instantly ruins the query.

## Approach

1. For each `query`, keep `matched`, the number of pattern letters matched so far, and a flag `ok`.
2. Walk the query with index `i`. If its letter `ch` equals `pattern[matched]`, advance `matched`.
3. Otherwise `ch` is an inserted letter: if it is uppercase, the query cannot match, so clear `ok` and stop.
4. After the scan the query matches only if `ok` is still true and `matched` reached `pattern.length`.

## Example 1, step by step

`pattern = "FB"`.

- `"FooBar"`: `F` matches (`matched = 1`), `o`, `o` are lowercase extras, `B` matches (`matched = 2`), `a`, `r` are extras: `true`.
- `"FooBarTest"`: same until `T`, an uppercase letter with nothing left to match: `false`.
- `"FootBall"` and `"FrameBuffer"` behave like `"FooBar"`: `true`.
- `"ForceFeedBack"`: `F` matches, then the second `F` is neither `B` nor lowercase: `false`.

The result is `[true, false, true, true, false]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(total length of all queries): every letter is looked at once.
- Space: O(number of queries) for the answer; the scan itself uses O(1).

## Pitfalls

- Do not forget the final check `matched === pattern.length`: `"Fo"` does not match `"FoBa"` even though it has no bad letters.
- Guard `matched < pattern.length` before comparing, so letters after the full pattern are treated as extras.
- Only lowercase letters may be inserted; an extra lowercase letter is fine, an extra uppercase letter is not.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `answer` | the list of booleans being built |
| `query` | the word being checked |
| `matched` | how many letters of `pattern` are already matched |
| `ok` | false once an extra uppercase letter is seen |
| `i`, `ch` | position and letter in the query |

narration.2: Start an empty list of answers, one per query.
narration.3: Check each query on its own.
narration.4: No pattern letter has been matched yet.
narration.5: Assume the query is fine until an extra uppercase letter shows up.
narration.6: Scan the query from left to right.
narration.8: If this letter is the next pattern letter, use it right away.
narration.9: One more pattern letter is matched.
narration.10: Otherwise the letter is an insertion; an uppercase insertion is not allowed.
narration.12: No need to look at the rest of this query.
narration.15: The query matches only if nothing bad was seen and the whole pattern was used.
narration.17: Return one boolean for every query.
